title: Björk, “All Is Full of Love” music video
lede: Chris Cunningham’s video of two white robots with Björk’s features, assembled and kissing in a clinical white room.
summary: Two white humanoid robots in a white, Japanese-styled lab. Directed by Chris Cunningham, 1999.

source.label: Wikipedia: All Is Full of Love

evidence.note: Based on Wikipedia and Media Art Net descriptions. No still of at least 800 px from a named copy was inspected.

styles.note: Partial fit: the humanoid robot and white-lab future of the period. The palette is white and clinical, not chrome or candy plastic.

context: The video was directed by Chris Cunningham and premiered in April 1999; post-production was by Glassworks. Cunningham described a white environment with “a Japanese feel to it”. It won MTV Video Music Awards for Breakthrough Video and Best Special Effects in 2000 and was on permanent exhibition at the Museum of Modern Art. [Wikipedia: All Is Full of Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Is_Full_of_Love).
Media Art Net describes two humanoid robots being assembled, kissing, and falling in love. [Media Art Net](http://www.medienkunstnetz.de/works/all-is-full-of-love/).
interpretation: The cyborg is one of the style’s image motifs. This video shows its sincere, tender version around 1999: the machine as beautiful, not threatening.
It is close to the white, minimal side of the period and is useful as an edge case for the Y2K rubric.
borrow: Pair white glossy surfaces with a cool, soft light to suggest a clean-room future.
